extraction.outputs: Checks, observations and command fields are copied from the redacted source report. Native stderr is omitted; stdout is unchanged.

isolation.homes: Independent temporary HOME/AW/Agent/XDG roots and project/neutral directories per scope.
isolation.clientInstallation: Exact public npm versions; scripts disabled; temporary prefixes removed.

qualificationBoundary.products: Only Gemini CLI 0.67.0 Project ordinary Skills in Linux, macOS and Windows x64/arm64.
qualificationBoundary.surface: Native extension installation and refresh, fresh enabled target and disabled neutral inventories, observed current Skill descriptions, removal and cleanup from the AW projection candidate.
qualificationBoundary.trust: Fixtures explicitly trust the isolated source and working directories. This does not authorize trust for another directory or user environment.
qualificationBoundary.activation: Project fixtures manually insert the !* default-disable rule before the exact project enable rule. These cells prove effective scope under that premise, not production AW automatic project activation.
qualificationBoundary.skillLoading: Skill discovery and refreshed descriptions are observed. Actual loading and model adoption remain unverified and do not block this limited management qualification.
qualificationBoundary.publicAw: No public AW Project pass is claimed. New Hosted public install/update/same-version dynamic consumer bytes/effective scope/remove validation must use the production activation writer without manual fixture activation.
qualificationBoundary.userEvidence: User qualification remains separately bound to native-gemini-skills-2026-11-12.json; no old record is rebound.
limitations: No prompts, model adoption or invocation-control qualification.
No MCP, Hook, Agent or Instructions execution qualification.
Only the six passed Project Native cells qualify. All six original reports and their Gemini client results remain failed; public AW failures are not overwritten.
Projection digests and observed Skill descriptions do not qualify full dynamic consumer byte equality through public AW.
Process receipts support only the recorded lifecycle and scope observations, not other Provider, OS or profile capabilities.
No extrapolation to User, App, another version, OS, architecture, component or feature.
